method.value: Draw individual YSOs and clusters from the IMF and CMF until the total population mass is reached; assign binary companions.

evidence.quote: individual YSOs and clusters are assigned to the population with masses drawn from the Initial mass function (IMF) and cluster mass function (CMF) until the total population mass is reached.

key_parameters.value: Total mass M_star, age t_0 and foreground extinction A_V.

evidence.quote: Under these assumptions, we can generate model populations with only three free parameters: total mass ($M_\star$), age ($t_0$, defined as time since the start of protostar formation), and foreground extinction ($A_V$).

assumptions.value: Kroupa IMF and modified turbulent-core accretion.

evidence.quote: We use the IMF from (cite: 2001Kroupa) that gives the probability distribution of individual star masses.
We thus focus on populations using turbulent-core accretion for the remainder of this work.

assumptions.value: Burst and continuous star formation histories.

evidence.quote: The first case is the burst model where all members of a population begin accreting at the same moment in time.
The other case is the continuous star formation history, where the ages of the individual sources is evenly distributed from the beginning of accretion to the current age of the population.

validation.value: Initial comparison of accretion histories against observed sources.

evidence.quote: our initial testing showed that the (cite: 2025Richardson) modified turbulent-core accretion was the most effective at replicating observed sources.

method.value: Match isolated YSOs to radiative transfer models in temperature-luminosity quantile space; combine cluster-member and intracluster-medium fluxes.

evidence.quote: For each isolated YSO, a model was randomly selected from the 10 nearest neighbors in temperature-luminosity quantile space (quantile transform fit to the temperature and luminosity of all models).
The final cluster flux in each filter is found by adding the flux contributions of all of the members and the intra-cluster medium.

key_parameters.value: Random inclination; largest aperture 10^6 AU for isolated YSOs.

evidence.quote: A random inclination is chosen, then the flux of that star was taken to be the flux in the largest aperture ($10^6$ AU) in each filter, given by the chosen model.

key_parameters.value: Reject model SEDs below 10 μJy at 21 μm and 1 μJy at 1.6 μm.

assumptions.value: Constant foreground extinction screen across each population.

evidence.quote: In this initial implementation, we adopt a simple screen along the line of sight with a constant extinction across the entire population.

assumptions.value: Flat priors over the sampled model parameter ranges.

evidence.quote: We adopt flat priors over the range of parameters sampled in our models (see above).

fitting.value: Sum log-probabilities of observed source counts across histogram grid points and sample the posterior with EMCEE.

evidence.quote: can be found by summing the log-probabilities at each grid point using the actual number of sources and the model PDFs.
This sampling is done using the Markov chain Monte Carlo package EMCEE (cite: 2013emcee).

validation.value: First two components contain approximately 97% of variance; folded normal distributions empirically outperform Poisson and normal distributions.

evidence.quote: these first two components contained $\approx97\%$ of the variance in the full sample.
We adopt the folded normal functional form based on a better empirical match to the population distributions than simpler forms like Poisson or normal distributions.

why_this_method.value: Use PCA because no single infrared color-magnitude or color-color diagram captures SED complexity.

evidence.quote: However, there is no single color-magnitude or color-color diagram in the infrared that can represent the complexity of the SEDs (cite: 2017Jones).
To discriminate between different YSO populations, we perform dimensionality reduction through PCA

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Other accretion histories were generated; modified turbulent-core accretion best replicated observed sources in initial testing.

evidence.quote: We generated populations using all of the accretion histories
our initial testing showed that the (cite: 2025Richardson) modified turbulent-core accretion was the most effective at replicating observed sources.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Folded normal distributions were preferred to Poisson and normal distributions.

evidence.quote: We adopt the folded normal functional form based on a better empirical match to the population distributions than simpler forms like Poisson or normal distributions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Continuous histories fit worse than burst histories for both N44 and NGC 604.

evidence.quote: We find that the probability of the continuous model generating the observed data is eight orders of magnitude worse than the burst model.
Again the continuous model is a worse fit with the total probability being 10 orders of magnitude worse than the burst model.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Use two components containing approximately 97% of variance and 10 histogram bins to balance resolution against small-number statistics.

evidence.quote: these first two components contained $\approx97\%$ of the variance in the full sample.
We adopted 10 bins to have sufficient resolution while avoiding small-number statistics.

limitations_admitted.value: Simplified star formation histories introduce systematic age uncertainty.

evidence.quote: In the absence of these more sophisticated star formation histories, the simple model will introduce systematic uncertainty into the age estimations.

limitations_admitted.value: Accretion varies smoothly in the implementation; stochastic accretion is not explored.

evidence.quote: Another important caveat is that the current implementation prescribes smooth variations in accretion, which differs from observed stochastic accretion (cite: 2023Fischer).
Our framework is capable of handling other varieties of accretion history, such as stochastic, but we do not explore those here.

limitations_admitted.value: F335M, F770W and F1130W may be poorly represented because PAH emission is not well simulated.

evidence.quote: specifically F335M, F770W, and F1130W, which are often dominated by polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons that are not well simulated in the models.

limitations_admitted.value: Low source counts and older ages limit age recovery; the lower mass prior boundary biases 1000 M_sun populations upward.

evidence.quote: However, lower mass populations with fewer sources do not give an accurate age prediction.
populations older than $\sim2$ Myr are indistinguishable from one another for $M_\star < 10^4~M_\odot$.
populations of $1000$ M$_\odot$ are predicted to have a systematically higher mass, which is due to $1000$ M$_\odot$ being the minimum allowed value in our flat mass prior.

limitations_admitted.value: N44 fits are affected by inconsistent SED coverage, catalog completeness and limited high-luminosity models.

evidence.quote: These inconsistent SEDs could be leading to inconsistent PCA fits shifting the number of sources contained at each grid point.
Second, the completeness of the YSO catalogs could be resulting in fewer than expected faint sources being included in the population fits.
Third, the models have limited models at very high luminosities, which could lead to our model populations not accurately representing the brightest observed sources.

limitations_admitted.value: The NIRCam-first catalog may omit deeply embedded sources.

evidence.quote: This catalog may be missing some deeply embedded sources that are mid-infrared bright and near-infrared dim.

limitations_admitted.value: Two regions are insufficient for rigorous conclusions about changing star formation histories.

evidence.quote: While no conclusions can be rigorously drawn from a sample of two regions

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA rejection cannot be audited without a detection threshold, velocity window and spatial association rule.
Self-fitting tests assess recovery within the generating model family, rather than robustness to incorrect physical assumptions.
The six-filter data description and the MIRI photometry filter list disagree: the latter includes F444W and omits F1130W.
Quoted posterior uncertainties should be distinguished from uncertainty in accretion history, cluster fraction, completeness and contamination.
The description does not explain how likelihoods are evaluated between sampled model grid points.

evidence.quote: We retrieved data from the public JWST program DDT 6555 (PI:M.G.Marin).

code_released.value: A full public PxP release is planned to accompany the future Milky Way analysis.

evidence.quote: A full public release of PxP is planned to accompany this Milky Way analysis.

missing_for_reproduction: A released PxP implementation and the exact modified stellar evolution code.
Numerical population-model settings, PCA transformations, histogram edges and fitted count-distribution grids.
MCMC configuration and definitions of reported central values and uncertainties.
Exact ALMA products and the CO-based rejection rule, including the identities of rejected candidates.
JWST reduction and photometry configuration, adopted distances and treatment of missing or mismatched filters.
The full machine-readable YSOC table, which is referenced but only partly supplied in this text.
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Cannot estimate ALMA data volume from the stated project code and transition alone.
reproducibility.score_reason: The paper provides numeric results, selection cuts and a substantial conceptual recipe, but exact ALMA screening, model settings and sampling details are missing; the full PxP release is deferred.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are numeric and JWST data are stated to be public, but ALMA public availability is not stated and the end-to-end recipe lacks essential code and settings.

methods_papers.why: DOLPHOT JWST/MIRI module, YSOC selection and model detectability cuts.
Modified accretion implementation and use of total luminosity.
Radiative transfer models and selected geometries.

companion_papers.why: First presentation and fuller description of the reduced NGC 604 JWST data.
Planned investigation of differences between accretion histories.
